questions.q: Why write down success criteria before building the model?
options: Azure ML refuses to start a job without them
They make the model train faster
They define what done means, so you can judge results objectively instead of after the fact
They replace the need for a baseline
questions.explain: Success criteria set before modeling keep the project honest: you test the result against them rather than choosing a flattering metric afterwards.

questions.q: With a 35% churn rate, a model that always predicts 'no churn' scores about 0.647 accuracy. What does that show?
options: Accuracy alone can look decent while finding zero churners, so it is a poor headline metric here
The model is well calibrated
The data is too small to model
Accuracy is always the best metric for imbalanced data
questions.explain: The baseline had zero recall and an AUC of 0.5. Metrics like AUC and recall expose what accuracy hides on imbalanced classes.

questions.q: Why keep scaling and one-hot encoding inside the scikit-learn Pipeline?
options: It is required by scikit-learn
It removes the need to test the model
It makes the model more accurate on every dataset
The deployed artifact is one self-contained model that accepts raw columns, avoiding train/serve mismatch
questions.explain: When preprocessing ships inside the model, an endpoint can accept raw feature columns and training-time and serving-time transformations cannot diverge.

questions.q: The retention team wants scores instantly on a support screen and in bulk every night. Which endpoint types fit?
options: Batch endpoint for both
Online endpoint for the instant scores and batch endpoint for the nightly list
Online endpoint for both, always
Neither; use a notebook
questions.explain: Low-latency single lookups suit real-time endpoints; large scheduled scoring suits batch endpoints.

questions.q: In this capstone, how are the cloud-only steps (registering in a workspace, creating endpoints) presented?
options: As output captured from a live Azure run
They are skipped entirely
As clearly labeled illustrative code adapted from Microsoft Learn, since no Azure account is used
As screenshots edited to match the project
questions.explain: No Azure account is available in the course, so cloud steps are illustrative and labeled, while everything runnable is run locally.
